text: Debugging is an important skill for any programmer. When your code does not work, the first step is identifying bugs. These are mistakes that cause your program to behave in unexpected ways. To find them, you can use debugging tools such as breakpoints and step-by-step execution. A systematic approach is also helpful: check your code carefully, test one part at a time, and make changes slowly. Logging is another useful method. By adding print statements or log messages, you can see what your program is doing and where it fails. With practice, debugging becomes easier and helps you write better code.
